name: the forest
title: A Quiet Forest
description: The forest begins in a close assembly of high trunks, whose crowns admit only a diminished light. The roar of the sea is already remote.
Tall trees stand so near one another that daylight reaches the ground in broken patches. Behind you, the ocean has sunk to a faint murmur.
Beneath the interlaced branches, the air is still and cool. Little remains of the coast's incessant noise, and the landward country is hidden among the trees.

text: Once more the trees gather about you, shutting out the noise of the sea.
You re-enter the forest beneath its lofty and closely spaced branches.
The sound of the coast diminishes as you pass under the trees.
Here the light is filtered through foliage, and the air scarcely moves.
The forest receives you again with its familiar stillness.
You return to the cool half-light beneath the canopy.
At night the forest is almost impenetrably dark. You proceed cautiously between the trunks.
The branches conceal what little light the sky affords; even your hands are hard to see.
Deep darkness gathers beneath the trees, obliging you to find your way by touch.
Fallen branches remain plentiful beneath the trees.
The forest floor is strewn with dry wood suitable for fuel.
Dead branches lie scattered among the roots, ready to be gathered.

From the interior comes a faint but persistent sound of running water.

The spring continues to issue from the moss-covered stones.
Clear water runs steadily between the rocks of the discovered spring.
Before the spring comes into view, its gentle murmur reaches your ears.

text: The trunks rise straight and close about you, with a dim green light filtering through their leaves.
In every direction the forest appears dense, cool, and scarcely disturbed by wind.
Roots, moss, and fallen branches cover the ground beneath the trees; the sea is almost silent here.
Dry limbs lie among the roots in quantities sufficient for several fires.
The trees have shed a considerable store of deadwood upon the forest floor.
Among the undergrowth you observe fallen branches, dry enough to serve as fuel.

view.text: Somewhere beyond the nearest trunks you hear the unmistakable movement of water over stone.
The spring continues to issue from the moss-covered stones.
Under the ferns, narrow passages run through the undergrowth, evidently used by small animals.

nothingLeft: No new feature distinguishes these trees from those already examined.
Your survey has, for the present, accounted for all that is readily visible here.
The remaining depths show only more trunks and undergrowth.

landmarks.label: the sound of water
text: Following the sound, you come upon a spring issuing between stones green with moss. Its water is clear and remarkably cold: a discovery of no small importance.
A little current wells up from the earth at the foot of a rock, then runs between mossy stones. Here is fresh water, apparently clean and easily obtained.
The source of the murmur proves to be a small spring, whose transparent water escapes between stones. The island has furnished one of the first necessities of life.

landmarks.label: the small trails
text: The narrow runs beneath the bracken bear fresh droppings and the marks of many small feet. Rabbits evidently use them; a few well-placed snares might provide meat.
On closer inspection the little trails prove to be worn by rabbits. The paths are so regular that a snare could be set across them with good prospects of success.
A network of passages through the low vegetation, together with fresh droppings, betrays the presence of rabbits. Cord and patience might turn these signs to advantage.

activities.name: chop wood
log: The axe bites deeply into a young trunk; chips scatter, and presently the tree falls.
You fell a slender tree and divide its trunk into lengths fit for building.
Repeated strokes open a deep cut in the wood until the trunk gives way.

activities.name: strip bark
log: You score the surface of a young tree and strip away long ribbons of inner bark.
The moist inner bark separates in tough, fibrous strips, each nearly an arm's length.
By alternating shallow cuts with careful pulling, you obtain a useful bundle of bark fibres.

activities.name: drink water
log: The spring water is exceptionally cold, with a faint mineral taste.
You cup the clear water in your hands and drink from the spring.
A trace of stone and moss flavours the fresh water.
You drink until the cold of the water sets your teeth aching.
You drink slowly from the spring, grateful for its constant supply.
Here, at least, the island offers fresh water without stint.
